rationale:
The single marked test, `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[installing_an_agent_after_discovery_preserves_the_cache]`, covers each obligation in `requirements.sdk.validation-cache.set_agent`.

- **Discover first, then select a model.** The test interns a node through the `discovery` clone before any agent exists. It asserts `discovery.2.agent.is_none()`. Agents are then installed afterwards.
- **The agent applies to subsequent requests through the handle and its future clones.** The test calls `set_agent(second)` and then clones `later`. It asserts that `later`'s agent is pointer-equal to `domain`'s agent. It then runs `Validator::verify` through `later` and asserts the result is `true`, which only the second backend returns. The second server is asserted to have received exactly one request.
- **Earlier clones keep their agent.** `earlier` is cloned after `set_agent(first)` and before `set_agent(second)`. After the second install, `earlier` still verifies to `false`, which only the first backend returns. The first server is asserted to have received exactly one request.
- **Node IDs are shared.** `later.cache().node_data(node)` returns the node interned through `discovery`, with `id == 9`.
- **Source snapshots are shared.** The test asserts `Arc::ptr_eq(&later.2.outlines, &discovery.2.outlines)`.
- **Aggregate usage is shared.** After one request through `earlier` and one through `later`, `discovery.cache().usage().attempts == 2`.

The assertions would fail if a later install changed an earlier clone, if the new agent did not reach future clones, or if the cache state were forked. I found no unmet obligation.

text: `set_agent` selects an agent for subsequent requests through this cache handle and its future clones. Earlier clones retain their selected agent. All handles continue to share the same node IDs, source snapshots, and aggregate usage. A caller can discover a graph before selecting the model for a review.
